content.value_statement: Vite projects need careful configuration across development, builds, plugins, and deployment. This skill gives concise guidance for common Vite workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains Vite config files, defineConfig, conditional config, and environment loading.
Guides dev, build, preview, SSR, library mode, and backend integration workflows.
Summarizes plugin usage, plugin hooks, virtual modules, and plugin ordering.
Covers CSS, assets, glob imports, HMR, web workers, and dependency pre-bundling.
Provides production build guidance for base paths, manifests, targets, and multi-page apps.
limitations: It does not run commands, install packages, or modify files by itself.
It reflects Vite 6.x content generated on January 28, 2026.
It gives guidance, but project-specific compatibility still needs testing.
It does not replace official Vite documentation for release-specific changes.

use_cases.title: Configure a Frontend App
use_cases.description: Set up Vite config, scripts, aliases, environment variables, and production build options.

use_cases.title: Build and Publish a Library
use_cases.description: Plan Vite library mode, entry points, file names, CSS output, and package exports.

use_cases.title: Integrate Vite with a Backend
use_cases.description: Connect Vite assets, manifests, dev server scripts, SSR output, and traditional backend templates.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Vite Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the safest Vite setup for a new React project. Include config files, scripts, and environment variable guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review Build Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Vite configuration goals for development, build, and preview. Tell me which options to use and why.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Plugins and Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Vite plugin setup for Vue, bundle analysis, and dependency pre-bundling. Include plugin order and common failure points.

prompt_templates.title: Design SSR and Library Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Vite architecture for SSR with library output and backend integration. Cover build steps, manifests, deployment, and testing checks.

output_examples.input: I need Vite environment variable guidance.
output: Use public prefixes only for values that can reach client code.
Use modes for staging and production differences.

output_examples.input: Help me improve a slow Vite dev server.
output: Use explicit import extensions where practical.
Review dependency pre-bundling and cache invalidation settings.

output_examples.input: I am building a Vite library package.
output: Choose entry points and output formats first.
Align package exports with generated build files.
Document CSS output and environment variable behavior for consumers.

best_practices: Keep Vite configuration small, explicit, and separated by development and production needs.
Expose only intended client environment variables through approved prefixes.
Test builds, preview output, SSR, and backend manifests before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not expose secrets through client environment prefixes.
Do not add plugins without checking order, scope, and build impact.
Do not rely on dev server behavior as proof of production correctness.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Vite commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for users to apply in their own projects.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it cover environment variables?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Vite modes, .env files, prefixes, and client exposure rules.

faq.question: Can it help with SSR projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers SSR development, builds, manifests, externals, and production server differences.

faq.question: Does it include plugin authoring guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers plugin hooks, virtual modules, order, and performance considerations.

faq.question: Is it tied to a Vite version?
faq.answer: Yes. The source states it is based on Vite 6.x content.
